claim: Former Suffolk County assistant district attorney who prosecuted major crimes and drug traffickers
finding: He joined the Suffolk DA's office after law school in 1998, rose to trial supervisor for the five East End towns, and left in 2004 for private practice in Mattituck.

claim: A lifelong resident of Suffolk County, born and raised on Long Island
finding: Raised in Patchogue (Patchogue-Medford High School). A Riverhead News-Review profile says he was born in Brooklyn, while Wikipedia lists Brookhaven. If Brooklyn is right, "lifelong Suffolk resident" overstates.

claim: First elected to the 2nd Assembly District in 2013 and served there several years
finding: Won the November 5, 2013 special election for the open AD2 seat with 57% and served until he moved to the Senate in 2021.

claim: Named Ranker on the Senate Codes and Ethics committees
finding: The Senate announced the appointment in January 2021. His Senate page now lists him as ranking member of Codes and Judiciary.

claim: As a freshman Assemblyman in 2013, sponsored and passed a law helping first-time homebuyers save thousands
finding: The law is real: his bill with Sen. LaValle exempting first-time buyers from Southold's Community Preservation Fund transfer tax passed both houses. It passed in June 2014, not 2013, and covers Southold only.

claim: His first bill was a tax cut that would save the average Suffolk resident over $2,500 a year
finding: The page names no bill and gives no basis for the figure. No record found.

claim: "Last year, he passed more bills than any other Republican Senator"
finding: The page gives no year. No ranking of bills passed by member was found.

claim: Has led the fight against cashless bail and the bail and discovery reforms
finding: His Senate releases document repeated bills and campaigns to roll back bail reform, including a 2024 bill with Assemblyman Durso.

claim: Supported and passed a constitutional amendment stripping corrupt politicians of their pensions
finding: The Legislature passed this amendment and voters approved it in 2017; he voted for it as an Assemblyman. "Passed" credits him with a measure the whole Legislature passed.

claim: Voted to suspend the state gas tax and restore STAR relief checks "this year alone"
finding: The gas-tax suspension was part of the 2022 state budget. The page doesn't give a year, so a 2026 reader would take these votes as recent.

claim: Leader in the movement to reform and repeal Common Core
finding: Advocacy claim; not measurable from public records.

claim: In his first Senate term, passed the Peconic Bay Region Community Housing Act
finding: His official Senate biography credits him with this bipartisan housing law.
